source.title: AI handles incidents, engineers lose touch with their systems
source.author: sylvainkalache

title.zh: AI事故响应与工程师能力退化
title.en: AI Incident Response and Fading SRE Skills

excerpt.zh: AI事故响应能降低常规故障的平均恢复时间，却可能让工程师失去排查系统的实践，团队需要用模拟演练保持复杂事故应对能力。
excerpt.en: AI incident response can reduce routine recovery time, but regular simulations are needed to preserve engineers’ ability to handle complex failures.

text.zh: AI事故响应带来的效率与风险
text.en: The Efficiency and Risk of AI Incident Response

text.zh: AI事故响应正在把许多原本需要值班工程师处理的工作自动化。根据这篇文章的描述，相关工具可以读取告警、提出故障假设、查询遥测数据、关联近期部署，甚至自行实施修复。它们处理夜间容量问题等常规事件时，确实可能减少打扰，并降低大多数事故的平均恢复时间。
text.en: AI incident response is automating work that once required on-call engineers. The article says these tools can inspect alerts, form hypotheses, query telemetry, correlate recent deployments, and even apply fixes themselves. For routine events such as an overnight capacity issue, that can reduce interruptions and may lower the average time to recovery for many incidents.

text.zh: 文章的核心担忧并不是自动化本身，而是人类与系统逐渐疏远。常规故障往往是工程师安全积累直觉的机会：他们能观察系统怎样退化、哪些信号具有价值，以及某个修复会带来什么副作用。当这些经历长期由模型完成，工程师可能越来越少亲手调查真实故障。
text.en: The central concern is not automation itself, but the growing distance between people and the systems they operate. Routine incidents are opportunities to build intuition: engineers learn how a system degrades, which signals matter, and what side effects a fix may create. When models handle those experiences for a long period, engineers may get far less practice investigating real failures themselves.

text.zh: 从常规故障到复杂事故
text.en: From Routine Failures to Complex Incidents

text.zh: 这形成了自动化悖论：工具越擅长处理正常情况，人类越可能只在异常、模糊且高风险的情况下接手。文章引用研究者Lisanne Bainbridge关于“自动化铁律”的观点指出，自动化会减少操作员练习日常工作的机会，却不会免除他们处理新问题的责任。因此，复杂事故的恢复时间未必与常规事故同步下降，甚至可能因为响应者缺乏经验而上升。
text.en: This creates an automation paradox: the better a tool handles normal conditions, the more likely humans are to take over only when a situation is ambiguous, unfamiliar, and severe. Citing researcher Lisanne Bainbridge’s work on the “ironies of automation,” the article argues that automation reduces opportunities to practice routine work without removing responsibility for novel problems. As a result, complex-incident resolution may not improve alongside routine recovery and could take longer when responders lack experience.

text.zh: 航空业被文章视为可借鉴的参照。飞行自动化承担了大量日常操作，但飞行员仍须面对发动机故障、仪表不可靠和失速等罕见情形。由于这些事件很少在真实飞行中出现，航空公司通过定期模拟器训练维持应急能力。软件事故通常不直接威胁生命，但快速理解不完整信息、作出取舍并协调团队，同样需要反复练习。
text.en: The article points to aviation as a useful comparison. Flight automation handles much routine operation, yet pilots remain responsible for rare events such as engine failures, unreliable instruments, and stalls. Because these situations are seldom encountered in real flights, airlines use recurring simulator training to preserve emergency skills. Software incidents usually do not threaten lives directly, but quickly interpreting incomplete information, making tradeoffs, and coordinating a team also require repeated practice.

text.zh: 事故模拟器如何补回实践
text.en: How Incident Simulators Restore Practice

text.zh: 文章介绍了一种面向软件团队的做法：让工程师在模拟的电商中断中担任事故指挥官，使用可观测性工具调查问题，同时与由LLM驱动的利益相关者在Slack中沟通。这样的训练不只考查技术定位，还要求参与者处理不完整证据、保持响应秩序、向管理层和客户支持团队传达信息，并在压力下推进决策。文中称，Rootly与Uptime Labs已围绕这一思路开展合作。
text.en: The article describes a software-focused approach: engineers take the incident commander role during a simulated e-commerce outage, use observability tools to investigate, and communicate with LLM-powered stakeholders in Slack. This tests more than technical diagnosis. Participants must work with incomplete evidence, keep the response organized, communicate with leadership and customer support, and make progress under pressure. The article says Rootly and Uptime Labs have partnered around this model.

text.zh: AI也可以充当教练，让响应者追问代理采取了哪些步骤、检查了哪些信号，以及诊断依据是什么。不过，解释仍不能取代操作经验。观察一个智能代理完成事故处理，或许能帮助工程师理解流程；真正形成能力，还需要他们亲自面对故障、承担判断后果，并在模拟环境中反复修正方法。
text.en: AI can also act as a coach by showing responders which steps an agent took, which signals it examined, and what evidence supported its diagnosis. Yet explanation is not a substitute for operating experience. Watching an intelligent agent resolve an incident may clarify a process, but durable skill requires engineers to face failures themselves, bear the consequences of decisions, and repeatedly refine their approach in a simulation.

text.zh: 把能力维护纳入值班准备
text.en: Making Skill Maintenance Part of On-Call Readiness

text.zh: 对团队而言，合理的方向不是放弃AI，而是把自动化和主动练习结合起来。值班准备可以包含定期事故模拟、桌面推演，以及经过设计的混沌工程活动，让工程师继续接触不熟悉的失效模式。训练也应覆盖事故指挥、沟通、升级和证据判断，而不只是记忆运行手册。AI可以生成角色、提供线索并复盘过程，但关键决策仍应由人完成。
text.en: For teams, the practical answer is not to abandon AI but to pair automation with deliberate practice. On-call readiness can include recurring incident simulations, tabletop exercises, and carefully designed chaos engineering so engineers continue to encounter unfamiliar failure modes. Training should cover incident command, communication, escalation, and evaluation of evidence, rather than only memorizing runbooks. AI can generate stakeholders, provide clues, and support reviews, while people still make the critical decisions.

text.zh: 这篇文章留下了一个值得持续验证的问题：当AI让常规事故更快恢复时，团队是否建立了足够的机制来防止“理解债务”累积？答案取决于组织是否把模拟训练视为生产可靠性的一部分，并用真实反馈调整难度和频率。自动化的价值不仅在于今天少处理几次告警，也在于系统失去自动化帮助时，人仍然能够理解它、控制它并恢复它。
text.en: The article leaves an important question for teams to test: when AI makes routine incidents faster to resolve, have they created enough structure to prevent “comprehension debt” from accumulating? The answer depends on whether simulation is treated as part of production reliability, with difficulty and frequency adjusted through feedback. Automation should not be judged only by how many alerts it removes today. Teams must also remain able to understand, control, and restore their systems when automated help is unavailable.
